links.note: Gives a straight, centrally loaded column's slenderness, Euler or Johnson critical stress and load, and its factor against your applied load.
Works out a full tank's weight and load per leg, then each tubular leg's slenderness, Euler or Johnson buckling load and factor for the K you choose.
Gives area, principal second moments and the least radius of gyration of I, T, channel and angle sections built from rectangles.
Supplies area, second moments and radii of gyration of rectangles, circles and tubes for use in the buckling checks; it gives no load capacity.
Calculates a column's crippling load by the Rankine–Gordon formula, with the theoretical or an empirical constant, and the factor on your load.
Puts the Euler load, Rankine–Gordon crippling load and the classic working-stress safe load side by side for one concentric strut.
Finds the peak stress in a column with an offset load by the secant formula, its Euler load, and the load factor at which it first yields.
Sizes a round bar or tube strut for a load and length: the least diameter for your factor, then the chosen size's slenderness, mode and factor.
Sizes a cylinder from its duty, including the least rod diameter for Euler buckling at the extended length and mounting factor you enter.
Checks the barrel, end cap and fully extended rod of a cylinder, with rod buckling checked against the full push at the working pressure.
Gives a screw's Euler buckling load and critical speed from its root diameter, unsupported length and end mounting, against your load and speed.
For a solid round bar heated between restraints: thermal stress and force, yield and buckling factors, and the temperature rise at which each is reached.
Gives the elastic collapse and yield-limited pressures of a long, unstiffened tube under external pressure, the governing mode and the wall needed.
Works out shear-leg geometry, the force in each leg, the thrust at each foot and each tube leg's buckling factor, with the foot tie checked.
Gives the first critical speed of a uniform shaft, alone and with one disc combined by Dunkerley, for simple, overhung or fixed supports, against running speed.
Estimates a simply supported shaft's first critical speed with up to three masses by Dunkerley's method, with a masses-only Rayleigh value for comparison.
Sizes a shaft for combined bending and torsion with shock factors, for a twist limit, and for a critical speed ratio, and says which criterion governs.
Turns a rigid rotor's mass, speed and balance grade into its permissible residual unbalance, per plane, and checks a measured residual against it.
Adds known unbalances as vectors, sizes and places a single-plane correction, and checks the residual left by weight steps and angle error against the grade.
Resolves up to three unbalance masses along a rotor into correction masses and angles in two chosen planes by taking moments.
Checks each correction plane's unbalance against the grade, gives the corrections and the rotating bearing forces, and checks the weights fit.
Gives the centrifugal force, acceleration in g and tangential speed of a mass rotating at a radius, such as a hammer on its pin.
Gives the maximum centrifugal stress in a flat solid or bored disc, its rim speed, factor against yield and the speed at which it would yield.
Works out a turning rotor's angular momentum, gyroscopic couple and bearing reactions, adds its weight, and flags a bearing load that reverses.
Gives a rotor's inertia, run-up time, revolutions and stored energy, and the heat a direct-on-line start puts into the motor per start and per hour.
Finds the torsional natural frequency of a two-inertia drive joined by a shaft and checks it against running-speed orders; coupling stiffness is added by hand.
Calculates a rolling bearing's outer race, inner race, roller spin and cage defect frequencies and matches a measured spectrum peak to them.
